segments.title: 第137章 溪溪的擔憂
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 137: Xixi's Worry

On the campus of No. 1 Affiliated High School, the academic buildings were practically empty, while the sports ground was abuzz with activity.

Sometime after nine in the morning, Li Luo called over Lin Yuan and Zhang Guohuang, who didn't have any events to compete in for the time being, and went to the school's perimeter wall at the edge of the sports ground.

He successfully got two large boxes of snacks from his uncle, Lin Xiufeng. They were all bought at wholesale price, so they didn't cost much.

After having Lin Yuan and Zhang Guohuang each carry a box back to the stands, Li Luo had Xiuxiu arrange for them to be distributed to their classmates, which was met with a round of cheers.

The students from the neighboring class watched with envy, but since this was a treat from the Class President of Class 8, they could only look on and feel a small pang of jealousy in their hearts.

For Li Luo, although he wasn't yet an adult and many avenues for making big money were still unavailable, an expense of a few hundred yuan like this was no longer any pressure for him at all.

It was nice to be able to make the people around him happy.

Compared to those who, in pursuit of a girl, spent heaps of money on bags, clothes, and cosmetics, dropping thousands or even tens of thousands without making a single ripple, his way was quite a bargain.

However, after distributing the snacks to everyone as Li Luo had instructed, Xiuxiu returned to her seat, took out an English vocabulary list, and began quietly memorizing words.

Beside her, Lin Yuan opened a sun umbrella and sat next to Xiuxiu, shading her from the sun so she could see the contents of the vocabulary list clearly without straining her eyes too much.

The other students in the class were whispering and laughing, but this scene was nothing out of the ordinary for them.

Only when Kong Junxiang occasionally came over to inspect and see what everyone was up to would Lin Yuan quietly close the umbrella, pretending like nothing happened.

And just like Xiuxiu, every class in the stands had a few study fiends who would study diligently even during the sports meet.

Besides Xiuxiu, Class 8 also had Lu Jiahao, Wei Chun, Jin Yuting, and Shi Yanran.

In contrast, the lively bunch like Zhu Yufei, Zhang Guohuang, and Xu Yinghuan walked around, eating, drinking, and having fun, laughing and joking. They were a completely different breed from the group above.

Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng were somewhere in between these two extremes.

They neither used this time to study nor ran around crazily having fun; they just sat in their seats watching the events.

When Yan Zhusheng was occasionally in the mood, she would play the harmonica for Li Luo for a while.

And ever since she heard that Li Luo could also write songs, Xu Yinghuan had been clamoring for Li Luo to sing.

Pestered endlessly by the girl, Li Luo had no choice but to have Yan Zhusheng play a simple accompaniment and sing "Follower of the Light."

After the song was finished, Xu Yinghuan led the applause, and many people from the neighboring class were also drawn over.

However, compared to Li Luo, they were clearly more interested in Yan Zhusheng. "Can you let the main singer next to you sing?"

Yan Zhusheng blinked, not really caring whether she sang or not. She just handed the harmonica to Li Luo, giving him a look that said, "Why don't you accompany me?"

Li Luo naturally chuckled and said to the students from the next class, "Wait until the closing ceremony to hear her. It costs money to listen privately."

"So that song just now was really written by our class president?" Xu Yinghuan leaned closer to Yan Zhusheng, asking with a face full of curiosity. "That's too amazing. I couldn't tell. Li Luo, why weren't you this amazing in middle school?"

"I suddenly had an epiphany, alright?" Li Luo's mouth twitched. He thought to himself that this song "Follower of the Light" was now wasted, at least in terms of using it in his book.

Otherwise, just within his class, he knew of at least Zhu Yufei and Zhang Guohuang who were reading his novel.

Who knew if the other boys in their dorm were also reading it?

If he wrote it into the book and was found out, he really wouldn't be able to clear his name even if he jumped into the Yellow River.

"Yan Zhusheng, Xu Yinghuan." Zhu Yufei, who had just finished the men's 100-meter race and bravely took first place in his group, returned to the stands and called out to them in their seats, "The 200-meter preliminaries are about to start. You two should get ready."

"It's your turn again," Li Luo said.

"It's a pity I didn't make it to the 100-meter finals," Xu Yinghuan sighed. Her preliminary time for the 100-meter race was only 13th, while Ying Chanxi managed to squeeze in at 8th place, barely making it.

As for Yan Zhusheng, it went without saying that she easily took first place, truly worthy of the woman who broke the school record in middle school.

"Zhusheng, before we go check in, will you go to the restroom with me?" Xu Yinghuan said, holding Yan Zhusheng's arm. "We can go straight to the gymnasium on our way back from the restroom."

"Okay," Yan Zhusheng nodded, looking at Li Luo before leaving.

Li Luo understood her meaning at a glance and stood up, patting his pants. "I'll go to the gymnasium and wait for you then. I'll cheer for you both."

Yan Zhusheng nodded. They had successfully communicated without a single word, and she teamed up with Xu Yinghuan to conquer the restroom dungeon.

Watching the two of them leave, Li Luo wasn't in a hurry. He slowly walked down from his seat, sidled up to Lin Yuan, and said, "Teacher Kong is here."

Before his words even faded, Lin Yuan reflexively closed the umbrella, then got up and went to the railing pretentiously, looking left and right before turning back in shame and anger. "Class President, you tricked me!"

"Here," Li Luo stuffed a pack of snacks into his hand. "Our Vice President has been studying hard. Go give her some energy."

"Oh, oh, okay..." Lin Yuan held the snacks, a hint of excitement on his face. Following Li Luo's suggestion, he quietly sat back down next to Xiuxiu.

As for what happened next, Li Luo didn't know.

He had already left the stands and was walking along the edge of the sports ground toward the gymnasium.

On the way, he passed the rostrum and saw Xu Youyu's figure on the stage. Li Luo stopped, then walked up the steps and greeted him.

"You don't have any duties this morning, right? Why are you still out and about?" Xu Youyu was currently giving instructions to two sports meet announcers. When he saw Li Luo come up, he raised an eyebrow and smiled.

"Yan Zhusheng has a race. As the class president, I have to go down and cheer for her."

"Don't just focus on cheering." Xu Youyu pointed at the massive pile of bulletins on the table. "Out of all 48 classes from first to third year, your class has submitted the fewest."

"You can't even read all of them even if we write this many." Li Luo looked at the basket of bulletins at their feet and was speechless. "You probably couldn't finish reading them even if you went on for three days and two nights straight."

"How could we read them all?" Xu Youyu rolled his eyes at him. "We only pick out the well-written ones to read."

As Xu Youyu spoke, the male announcer over there had already picked out a decent one and begun to recite it with great emotion.

Li Luo felt goosebumps rise. His mouth twitched, and then he asked, "With 48 classes, how many of these do you read in a day? On average, each class only gets a few read."

"We have to broadcast other things too. Reading these is mainly to fill the empty time," Xu Youyu said with his arms crossed. "Over the two and a half days, we'll probably read a hundred or so."

"So that's only three or four per class?" Li Luo raised an eyebrow.

"This is a task assigned by the school. Can you not slack off?"

"How could I slack off, President?" Li Luo said with a grin. After the male announcer finished his recitation, he beckoned to him, signaling for the microphone.

The student froze for a moment, then looked at Xu Youyu.

"Ahem... give it to him," Xu Youyu glanced at Li Luo and said to the male announcer, then added a reminder, "What do you want the microphone for?"

"To read a bulletin, of course," Li Luo said as he took the microphone. After coughing twice to clear his throat, he turned the microphone on.

"On this green field, the flames of youth burn brightly."

"The sports meet is not just a contest of speed and strength, but a feast of spirit and will."

"Every athlete is a gust of wind on the track, a fierce tiger in the field, embodying the athletic spirit of 'higher, faster, stronger' through their actions."

"Teamwork, personal breakthroughs, every cheer, every embrace, is the most sincere tribute to the spirit of sports."

"The sports meet is not just a stage for competition, but a place where spirits soar. Let us witness this ode to youth together!"

Mimicking the male announcer's tone, Li Luo finished reciting this impromptu piece with passion, then returned the microphone with both hands. "President, how was that bulletin? It should at least get a passing grade, right?"

Xu Youyu: "...That's still just one."

"I'll come back this afternoon," Li Luo raised his eyebrows. "Same for tomorrow and the day after. I'll take care of our class's quota, and it'll save everyone the trouble of submitting shoddy work just to fill the numbers."

"I really don't know what to do with you," Xu Youyu placed his right hand on his forehead and sighed. "You're so capable, why don't you just take care of all the bulletins? It would save me the trouble of having people chase after every class."

"I can't do that," Li Luo shook his head repeatedly. "I'm busy. I'm taking off now."

After escaping from Xu Youyu, Li Luo finally made his way to the gymnasium.

Yan Zhusheng and Xu Yinghuan had already finished their trip to the restroom and arrived. Upon seeing Li Luo, Yan Zhusheng said with a curious look, "I think I heard your voice just now."

"I was roped into being a literary conscript," Li Luo shrugged, taking her harmonica from her hand and tucking it into his pocket.

After a simple check-in and queuing up, Yan Zhusheng and Xu Yinghuan soon followed the line onto the field.

Thanks to the ID tag around his neck, Li Luo had unrestricted access and followed them to the starting line of the 200-meter track.

As the starting pistol fired, Li Luo watched Yan Zhusheng's figure sprint away while casually strolling toward the 200-meter finish line.

As expected, he watched Yan Zhusheng's dashing figure cross the finish line.

After the men's 200-meter preliminaries were also over, it was noon.

Ying Chanxi and Qiao Xinyan found Li Luo and the others, and they all headed to the cafeteria for lunch.

"Li Luo, don't go yet." Ying Chanxi had Qiao Xinyan take a picture of them first, then took group photos with Yan Zhusheng, Xu Yinghuan, and Jin Yuting.

Finally, it was Li Luo's turn.

After Ying Chanxi tilted her head, leaned close to Li Luo's body, and successfully had their picture taken, Jin Yuting asked curiously from the side, "Xixi, when did you get a new camera?"

"Li Luo gave it to me," Ying Chanxi smiled happily, shaking the Polaroid in her hand. "The photo develops just a little while after you take it. It's very convenient."

"This seems pretty expensive," Jin Yuting glanced at the Polaroid and couldn't help but say, "I remember my cousin has one. It costs several thousand, and the film is super expensive too. One sheet costs several yuan. You just spent tens of yuan on these few pictures."

Hearing Jin Yuting say this, Ying Chanxi suddenly snapped to her senses, realizing something, and turned to look at Li Luo.

Because she usually had living expenses and pocket money from Ying Zhicheng, she didn't have a clear sense of consumption for things costing several thousand yuan.

But now, reminded by Jin Yuting, Ying Chanxi suddenly thought about how Li Luo's family was burdened with a mortgage. Where did he get the money to buy such an expensive camera?

Could it be from his uncle and auntie?

And if his uncle and auntie found out this was a gift for her... and it cost several thousand... Ying Chanxi bit her lip and instantly fell silent, a subtle panic rising in her heart.

At this moment, Li Luo was still completely oblivious and didn't notice the change in Ying Chanxi's expression at all. He just said, "It's just a gift. Talking about money ruins the sentiment. Let's hurry up and eat. I'm starving."

(End of Chapter)
